content.overview: A tort is a civil wrong, other than breach of contract, for which the remedy is an action for unliquidated damages or an injunction. Indian tort law is largely uncodified common law received through justice, equity and good conscience, supplemented by statutes such as the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

sections.heading: Meaning and scope
sections.body: Tort law protects private rights in personam. The claimant seeks compensation or restraint, not punishment as the primary object (though exemplary damages may occasionally be awarded). Distinguish tort from crime (public wrong; State prosecution; BNS offences) and from contract (consensual obligation; liquidated or unliquidated damages under contract rules).

sections.heading: Sources in India
sections.body: There is no general Indian Tort Code. Courts apply English common-law principles as adapted to Indian conditions, constitutional values (especially Articles 14, 21, 32 and 226 for constitutional torts), and subject-specific statutes. Always state whether the claim is pure common-law tort, statutory liability, or public-law compensation.

sections.heading: Track B — Chamber anchors
sections.body: Forum: ordinarily the civil court of competent territorial and pecuniary jurisdiction under the CPC; specialised forums include MACT (Motor Vehicles Act) and consumer commissions (CPA 2019). Limitation: typically Article 113 of the Limitation Act, 1963 (three years when the right to sue accrues) unless a special statute provides otherwise. Plead: material facts of duty/right, breach/wrong, damage, and relief (Order VI Rule 2 CPC). Evidence: BSA burden rules (ss. 104–106); electronic records need s. 63 foundation where applicable.

sections.heading: Revision
sections.body: Tort = civil wrong → unliquidated damages/injunction. Not crime, not mere contract breach. Indian law = common law + statutes + constitutional tort jurisprudence.

examples.title: Civil vs criminal defamation
examples.body: A false publication may support a tort claim for damages and, separately, a BNS s. 356 prosecution. The civil suit does not depend on conviction; standards of proof and remedies differ.

enhancement.definition: Tort is a civil wrong, independent of contract or breach of trust, for which the usual remedy is an action for unliquidated damages.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Tort law protects legally recognised interests through duties imposed by law rather than consensual agreement.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Indian tort law is largely uncodified. The governing rules are developed through common-law principles, Indian judicial decisions and applicable legislation for particular fields; no statute should be treated as a general codification of this topic.
essentialIngredients: A legally protected interest or right
A wrongful act or omission recognised by law
Legal damage or infringement, where required by the tort

distinctions.title: Tort vs contract
distinctions.left: Tort vs contract: tort duty is imposed by law; contractual duty arises from agreement.
distinctions.right: Apply the stated distinction to the facts.

distinctions.title: Tort vs crime
distinctions.left: Tort vs crime: tort primarily protects private rights and ordinarily leads to civil remedies; crime is a public wrong prosecuted by the State.
distinctions.right: Apply the stated distinction to the facts.
